fair_value_reason: Restating the agents' EPS from the 14-week x4 run-rate to a 13-week basis (~$10.6 run-rate, ~$11.0 FY27 for 53 weeks, ~$10.6-11.2 NTM by Oct 2027) and fixing agent_1's book value (~$66 per diluted share by late 2027, not $61) gives agent fair values of ~$98/$95/$96/$96/$91, mean ~$95. I take $96: ~9x NTM EPS of ~$10.7 blended with mid-cycle earnings power (~$7-7.5 x 12-13x), on ~86M diluted shares and $3.06B reported net debt. That is ~10% below the $106.94 price.
supervisor_summary: Round 2 shows the agents made and mostly verified every round-1 correction (Nov 4 report date, ~86M diluted shares, labelled net debt, primary-sourced credit, insider and recession data). But all five, following my round-1 file, annualized a 14-week Q1 guide into a '$11.40 run-rate'. On a 13-week basis it is ~$10.6, matching consensus, so AVT trades at ~10x real run-rate earnings, not ~9.4x, and underlying sequential growth into Q1 is ~2-3%, not 10%. Correcting it lowers reconciled fair value to ~$96 (about 10% below $106.94), the thesis break to $66, and the 12-month ladder by 1-2 points per strike (P>=107 0.44). The Nov 4 print, just outside the 1-month window, will show a 13-week Q2 guide that may look like a sequential decline on reported numbers.
key_drivers: Q1 FY27 guide of $9.0-9.3B / $2.80-2.90 covers a 14-week quarter; on 13 weeks that is ~$8.5B and ~$2.65, a run-rate of ~$10.4-10.6 that matches the ~$10.5 FY27 consensus, so the stock is ~10x real run-rate earnings, not ~9.4x
Multiple at peak-cycle earnings: ~10x today against ~6x adjusted EPS at the FY23 peak; GAAP EPS fell 34% in FY24 and 49% in FY25 after the last peak (EDGAR XBRL)
Price and inventory content of growth: Avnet sales +48% y/y while WSTS sees analog +10% and discretes +8% in 2026; memory ~1/3 of Q4 growth; receivables +$2.6B and inventories +$0.9B in FY26
Working-capital leverage: FY26 OCF -$280.9M, net debt $3.06B (forward ~$3.35-3.5B), ratings Baa3/BBB-/BBB- (one notch above high yield), in-the-money convert adds ~3.2M net shares at $107
Nov 4 print and Q2 (13-week) guide: likely to look flat or down sequentially on reported numbers; how the market reads it is the first test
